extracted.intended_audience: researchers submitting to eLife (authors) and potential peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Describes eLife's peer review and publishing model (Reviewed Preprints, eLife Assessments, Public Reviews), the roles of editors and reviewers, and procedural requirements for submission, revision, and publication. Intended to guide authors and reviewers on what to expect and what eLife evaluates and publishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewed Preprint publication model (no accept/reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing with eLife is different because there is no accept or reject decision after peer review: rather, every article we review is published as a Reviewed Preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Reviewed Preprint includes the preprint itself, the eLife Assessment, Public Reviews that describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and a response from the authors (if available). By making the views of expert editors and reviewers an integral part of the published paper, eLife aims to improve assessment of research. Reviewed Preprints can be cited by their DOI and/or their eLife citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife Assessment — significance of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife Assessments use a common vocabulary to summarise the significance of the findings reported in an article (on a scale ranging from landmark to useful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assessment should summarise the importance of the work for readers; editors and reviewers collaborate when writing Assessments. The significance label is published with the Reviewed Preprint and is intended to help readers and funders judge the contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife Assessment — strength of the evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife Assessments use a common vocabulary to summarise the strength of the evidence (on a scale ranging from exceptional to inadequate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assessment should evaluate how well the data support the claims. Strength-of-evidence labels are published alongside the significance label to give a concise judgment of the reliability and robustness of the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Reviews should state strengths, weaknesses, and whether claims are justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Reviews describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and indicate whether the claims and conclusions are justified by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each peer reviewer is asked to write a Public Review of the article, and to recommend ways in which the authors could improve it. Where the reviewers disagree with the claims in an article, this is made explicit within the eLife Assessment and the Public Reviews. Recommendations to the authors for improving the article are published as part of the Version of Record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewers must recommend improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each peer reviewer is asked to ... recommend ways in which the authors could improve [the article].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Reviews should be constructive and suggest concrete actions for authors to strengthen the manuscript; these recommendations are published with the article (and updated if a revised version is submitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife editors — who are all active researchers — discuss new submissions and decide which will be peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific criteria editors use are described in the linked page 'How and why eLife selects papers for peer review.' Selection is a gatekeeping step: only submissions chosen by editors proceed to peer review and become Reviewed Preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor and reviewer consultation during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers consult with each other during the peer-review process, especially when writing eLife Assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative discussion among editors and reviewers informs the Assessment and helps ensure the published evaluation reflects collective expert judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components and updates of a Revised Version
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are free to submit a revised version of their article, and the editor and the peer reviewers will update the eLife Assessment and the Public Reviews as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Version two of the Reviewed Preprint will include the revised preprint, an eLife Assessment and Public Reviews (updated as appropriate), and a response from the authors. This documents how the work and its evaluation have changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to publish a Version of Record (VOR)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any point following peer review, the authors can choose to publish their article as a regular journal article (the Version of Record) to mark the end of the review and publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of a VOR complies with major funder requirements for immediate online access. VORs are typically indexed by services (Google Scholar, PubMed, PubMed Central, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, DOAJ), but indexing is subject to each service's criteria and is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint transfer and preprint availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit to eLife directly or transfer a preprint from bioRxiv or medRxiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife works with authors to make all submissions selected for peer review available as preprints, combining advantages of preprints with peer-review scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee and waiver policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our publication fee is $3000 and is payable at this stage (although the fee is waived for anyone who cannot afford to pay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee is collected at the peer review/publication stage; authors who cannot afford the fee may request a waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about reviewer disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reviewers disagree with the claims in an article, this is made explicit within the eLife Assessment and the Public Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disagreements are published so readers can see the range of expert opinion rather than a single edited consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limits on number of articles reviewed or published
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not artificially limit the number of articles we review or publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's model is designed to focus on the scientific content rather than restricting volume of publications; selection is based on editorial criteria, not quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funders' recognition and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: An increasing number of funders are also recognising Reviewed Preprints in research assessment. Publication of an eLife Version of Record (VOR) complies with all major funding agency requirements for immediate online access to the published results of their research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider funder policies when choosing to publish a VOR; eLife's workflows are designed to meet common funder open-access mandates.
